title: Trump’s unprovoked attack on Iran has no mandate – or legal basis
description_short: Trump’s unprovoked attack on Iran has no mandate – or legal basis
description_medium: Trump’s unprovoked attack on Iran has no mandate – or legal basis. US president violates UN charter just days into his Board of Peace era, and chooses to take the biggest gamble of his administration This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: On February 28, 2026, the Guardian described U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran as an attempt at regime change launched while diplomatic efforts to avert conflict were underway. The article recounted Trump’s recorded address after the first bombs had fallen: he warned that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps should surrender or be killed, threatened to destroy the country’s armed forces, missiles, and navy, and urged Iranians to help bring down the government. The Guardian argued that the operation had no legal foundation and involved little consultation with Congress or the public. That is the article’s legal and political assessment, not a court ruling. The supplied account does not give the administration’s full legal rationale or establish the status of congressional authorization. The reporting supports describing the strikes, Trump’s stated objectives, and the Guardian’s criticism, while keeping the legal conclusion attributed to the outlet.

title: Trump boasts of a 'golden age' in State of the Union amid sharp partisan divisions
description_short: Trump boasts of a 'golden age' in State of the Union amid sharp partisan divisions
description_medium: Trump boasts of a 'golden age' in State of the Union amid sharp partisan divisions. More than 30 congressional Democrats boycotted President Trump's State of the Union address. Others attended alternative events. This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: President Donald Trump delivered the State of the Union address on February 25, 2026, and described the country as entering a “golden age.” The Los Angeles Times reported that more than 30 congressional Democrats boycotted the speech while others attended alternative events. Some lawmakers said they did not want to legitimize the address; others showed opposition inside the chamber or brought guests affected by the administration’s policies. Senator Alex Padilla delivered a rebuttal emphasizing different priorities on prices, voting access, and immigration enforcement. The report also described visible interruptions during Trump’s remarks, including protests over federal agents’ killings of Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Some Democrats remained seated while Trump spoke; others shouted “liar” and “corrupt,” and Representative Al Green was escorted from the chamber. These details show a sharply divided response to the address, but they do not establish that every absent lawmaker shared the same reason for boycotting it.

title: Trump calls justices 'fools,' announces new 10% global tariff after Supreme Court setback
description_short: Trump calls justices 'fools,' announces new 10% global tariff after Supreme Court setback
description_medium: Trump calls justices 'fools,' announces new 10% global tariff after Supreme Court setback. Trump told reporters that his administration will impose new tariffs by using alternative legal means. This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: On February 20, 2026, after the Supreme Court struck down his use of emergency powers for international tariffs, Donald Trump called justices who opposed the policy “fools” and “lapdogs.” Later that day, he signed an executive order imposing a new 10% tariff under a 1974 law. The Los Angeles Times reported that this authority limited the tariffs to 150 days unless Congress extended them. Trump described the court decision as a technical setback and said he would pursue other legal routes. The article also discussed possible future authorities, including a separate trade law; those options were legal possibilities, not all measures already imposed. The report confirms a signed tariff order, but the supplied record does not establish its effective date, product coverage, or economic cost. The episode paired Trump’s attack on the Court with an effort to continue tariff policy under a different statute.

title: Dinner with Nick Fuentes - Dining with Holocaust Deniers
description_short: Trump hosted dinner at Mar-a-Lago with Nick Fuentes, a prominent white supremacist and Holocaust denier
description_medium: On November 22, 2022, Donald Trump had dinner at Mar-a-Lago with rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and guests Ye brought, including Nick Fuentes, a white nationalist and Holocaust denier. NBC reported that the group discussed politics and that Ye asked Trump to be his running mate. Trump later said he did not know Fuentes or his background.
description_long: NBC News reported that Donald Trump met Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, for dinner at Mar-a-Lago on November 22, 2022. Ye brought three guests: Nick Fuentes, a white nationalist and Holocaust denier; Florida political operative Karen Giorno; and an unnamed parent of a student at Ye’s Donda Academy. People familiar with the conversation told NBC that Ye asked Trump to be his running mate and discussed politics, including January 6. They said Fuentes praised Trump and criticized Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, while Trump reportedly criticized Ye’s former wife, Kim Kardashian. Trump later said he did not know Fuentes or his background, and Fuentes confirmed Trump did not know he would attend. NBC reported that Trump and Ye had been speaking privately for weeks, but that does not establish what Trump knew about Ye’s guests in advance. The story identifies the three guests Ye brought; it does not provide a complete attendance list for the club’s dining area.
